Several strong open‑source Opsgenie alternatives exist in 2025, offering on‑call scheduling, alert routing, and incident management without vendor lock‑in. The most capable options include Iris, OnCall, OpenDuty, Cabot, and Grafana OnCall. Each caters to slightly different infrastructure and team‑size needs.

Notable Open‑Source Opsgenie Alternatives
Tool	Overview	Best For
Tool	Overview	Best For
Iris (LinkedIn)	High‑scale incident communication platform used internally at LinkedIn. Routes alerts intelligently to correct responders. Integrates tightly with OnCall.	Enterprise DevOps and SRE teams needing scalable, extensible alert routing 
.
LinkedIn OnCall	Handles complex on‑call schedules, rotations, and escalations. Integrates with Slack and email for customizable delivery.	Engineering teams managing multi‑team schedules with self‑hosted control 
.
OpenDuty	Lightweight, PagerDuty‑style alerting system using Twilio and SMTP for notifications.	Small teams seeking simplicity and control with minimal infrastructure 
.
Cabot	Combines uptime monitoring, health checks, and alerting in a single self‑hosted app. Integrates with popular monitoring tools.	Teams preferring an all‑in‑one open‑source monitoring and alerting stack 
.
Grafana OnCall (Community Edition)	Fully integrated with Grafana, Prometheus, and Loki. Supports escalation policies, scheduling, and Slack notifications.	DevOps orgs already using Grafana stack for observability 
.
Key Considerations
Hosting & Maintenance: All options require internal hosting, updates, and security configuration—unlike SaaS tools such as PagerDuty or TaskCall.

Integrations: Grafana OnCall and Iris/OnCall offer the most native integrations with modern observability stacks.

Status of Grafana OnCall OSS: Community reports note Grafana OnCall OSS has recently been deprecated, though forks and older versions remain available.

For teams prioritizing freedom from licensing constraints and deep operational customization, Iris + OnCall, Cabot, and OpenDuty are the leading open‑source alternatives to Opsgenie in late 2025.
